headline.purpose: Item-screen h1 (an assumption, a source). The largest type in the app.

title.purpose: Sheet title: the h1 of a list screen, followed by a faint count.

reading.purpose: Passages, quotes and empty-state text people read.

body.purpose: The UI: rows, buttons, menus, forms.

meta.purpose: Secondary lines, chips, hints, errors, group headings.

label.purpose: Counts, panel section labels, captions, keyboard hints.

card-pitch.purpose: Card kit only: the promise in one line on the concept's front, 19 to 28px with the card's width, its key phrase on a marker band.

card-heading.purpose: Card kit only: h1 and h2 on a front.

card-voice.purpose: Card kit only: a quote in the users' words, unattributed.

card-lede.purpose: Card kit only: the line under the pitch, muted; a measure's values.

card-name.purpose: Card kit only: a person's or a step's name.

card-subheading.purpose: Card kit only: h3 and h4, a measure's caption, a timeline's time.

card-body.purpose: Card kit only: running text, a shift's lists, a comparison.

card-detail.purpose: Card kit only: what a person needs, a step's line, a spectrum's ends, a note.

card-chip.purpose: Card kit only: a chip's label.

card-label.purpose: Card kit only: a small faint caption.

shadows.name: shadow
shadows.purpose: Resting: panels, sheets, the pill, callouts, the current segmented item. Dark: 0 2px 5px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.4), 0 0 0 0.5px rgb(255 255 255 / 0.08).

shadows.name: shadow-2
shadows.purpose: Lifted: menus, dialogs, toasts, panels as phone drawers. Dark: 0 10px 28px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.55), 0 0 0 0.5px rgb(255 255 255 / 0.1).

shadows.name: shadow-flash
shadows.purpose: The search palette alone, for a moment, when left untouched for three seconds; it fades back to shadow-2. Dark: 0 0 0 1px rgb(255 255 255 / 0.85), 0 0 0 7px rgb(255 255 255 / 0.3), 0 0 90px 28px rgb(255 255 255 / 0.35).

shadows.name: shadow-paper
shadows.purpose: The preview frame for an uploaded original. Dark: 0 0 0 1px rgb(255 255 255 / 0.08), 0 1px 3px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.3).

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: The one easing curve for every transition and entrance.

motion.name: dur-1
motion.purpose: Small state changes: hovers, carets, menus (menus close in 100ms).

motion.name: dur-3
motion.purpose: Panels, the inspector, the canvas and the pill.

motion.name: dur-4
motion.purpose: Layout that moves what is below it: an Idea card's text unfolding, the picture moving down in step. It folds back in dur-3 (200ms).

motion.name: ease-fold
motion.purpose: The fold's ease: a gentle start so a layout move reads rather than jumps, then a long settle. The app animates the measured height with it, so a reversal runs from wherever the fold is. None with reduced motion.

motion.name: idea-text-words
motion.purpose: The words in an Idea card's text arriving a beat behind their room; on closing they fade in 120ms first. With reduced motion only the fade remains.

motion.name: idea-reorder
motion.value: others glide 240ms, the released card 200ms, shared ease; the held card follows the pointer at 102% on the Lifted shadow
motion.purpose: Dragging outcomes into order, or moving a picked-up card with the keyboard. None with reduced motion, except the held card following the pointer.

narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Studio"**

One floating panel carries the product's whole story, Idea, Evidence, Exploration and Story in that order, and the content takes the rest of the canvas. Studio is a tool-maker's workspace: a light grey canvas (near-black in dark), white panels with 12px corners floating 10px in from the window edge, hairline rules, and a soft two-layer shadow. There is no top bar, no persistent rail beside the panel, and no app-level tab strip. One screen shows at a time, links are real links, and the browser owns tabs.

The system is dense and quiet. The UI runs at 12px in Inter; text people actually read (a source's text, quotes, Markdown) steps up to 13 to 13.5px. Hierarchy comes from weight (600) and grey steps rather than size, and nothing in the app is larger than 20px except the overview's intro. Indigo is the only chromatic voice in the chrome, reserved for selection, focus, primary commits and pointing at evidence. Status always pairs a small shaped mark with a word.

The panel can hide (a button or Ctrl/Cmd+\). The canvas widens in a single 200ms motion and a small floating pill with the mark takes its place. Item screens (a Story page, a mockup, a source) add a 272px inspector floating on the right, which hides and returns the same way: a button in its head or Shift+Ctrl/Cmd+\, and a square at the top-right inset in its place. A Story page is not part of Studio: it follows the product's own Story style (the company's design system or a house style) inside a sandboxed frame. Neither is a mockup's page, which carries its own look in the same kind of frame, nor an Idea card's front, a picture drawn in the card kit (its own section below) inside a sandboxed frame, in a card whose chrome is Studio. On the Story and on a mockup (on a phone too), focus mode (F) hides both panels so the app falls away around the work; a Story page keeps its measure rather than widening, and Esc or F brings the panels back.
keyCharacteristics: A 264px floating left panel and 272px floating inspector around one scrolling canvas (content max 900px; a mockup's canvas takes the full width).
White-on-grey tonal layering; the shadow's 0.5px ring stands in for a panel border.
Inter at 11 to 15px for the UI, 20px as the ceiling outside the overview's intro; 600 is the heading weight.
Indigo for selection, focus, primary commits and evidence only.
Lucide icons at 12 or 14px with a 1.75 stroke, through one glyph map.
Light and dark are both first-class and resolved before first paint.
Idea cards with two sides: an agent-drawn picture on the front, always in view, and the text agents read on the back, which More info opens between the card's title and its picture.

rules.name: The Earned Accent Rule
rules.body: Indigo means "selected, focused, commit, or evidence". It never decorates, never fills a header, and never marks a category. A view carries at most one accent-filled button, usually the commit in a form or dialog or the first-creation action in an empty state. A populated sheet header's create action stays a default button.

rules.name: The Mark And Word Rule
rules.body: Status is a 7px mark followed by a word, both in the status colour. The mark's shape carries the state on its own: a filled dot for positive, a ring for attention, a small diamond for negative, a spinning open arc for progress and a faint ring for neutral. Colour is never the only signal.

rules.name: The Two Schemes Rule
rules.body: Every colour token has a light and a dark value, and colour-mixed tokens are re-derived inside each theme scope. A new colour lands in both sets or it doesn't land.

rules.name: The Twenty Pixel Ceiling Rule
rules.body: Nothing in the app exceeds 20px. When something needs more emphasis, raise its weight or darken its grey. The one exception is the overview's intro (Brand and Display above, tokens `--fs-brand`, `--fs-display` and their `-sm` narrow sizes, `--tracking-brand`, `--tracking-display`), the page people share as a screenshot of WhatBuild; no other screen earns it ([decision](okf/decisions/the-overview-is-the-front-door.md)). An Idea card's front is not app type: it is a picture in the card kit, which may run its pitch to 28px, as a Story page has its own type. The card's head, More info and text stay under the ceiling.

rules.name: The Read Up Rule
rules.body: Chrome stays at 12px. Anything a person reads as content (passages, quotes, prose) steps up to 13 to 13.5px with a looser line height and a 68ch measure.

rules.name: The Whole Word Rule
rules.body: A title kept to one line takes its own direction and, when it is too long, ends in an ellipsis after its last whole word that leaves room for it, in reading order, so a title that mixes English and Arabic keeps the words it begins with. It still starts at the left. The whole title is read by assistive technology and shown on hover. Cut with OneLine, never with text-overflow.

rules.name: The One Scroller Rule
rules.body: The canvas scrolls the page. Only the panel's context slot, the inspector body, menus, dialogs and an Idea card's back (and a front taller than its frame) scroll on their own.

rules.name: The Float Inset Rule
rules.body: Floating surfaces sit exactly 10px from the window edge. On phones they go flush, never partially inset.

rules.name: The Two Heights Rule
rules.body: A surface either rests in the layout or lifts above it. Use no other shadow values, and use no offset or coloured shadows. The one exception is the search palette's passing flash.

rules.name: The One Hue Rule
rules.body: A card keeps to one hue for the product's way, chosen with `data-hue`. Slate, hatched, is how things are today. Rose is only for what hurts, a step or a moment marked as pain, and sparingly. Otherwise green, amber and rose appear only as a comparison's yes, partly and no, each with its own shape. Never a rainbow.

rules.name: The Picture Not Chrome Rule
rules.body: The kit's hues and sizes stay inside a front. The Earned Accent Rule governs Studio's chrome and is unchanged: the kit's indigo is the default hue of a sandboxed picture, not chrome, and never counts as a view's accent. No Studio surface borrows a kit hue.

rules.name: The Marker Band Rule
rules.body: Emphasis in a pitch (`em`, or `wb-mark` elsewhere) is a band of the hue's solid, about 30%, across the lower part of the words; the text stays in ink. A pitch never turns its key phrase a colour.

dos: **Do** take every colour, size, radius, shadow, duration and layer from the token file. Screen stylesheets compose tokens and add layout only.
**Do** keep controls at 24px or 28px, and reserve 32px for the floating pill and its square.
**Do** draw icons through the glyph map: lucide at 12px or 14px, 1.75 stroke, faint or muted at rest.
**Do** pair every status with its shaped 7px mark and a word.

**Do** animate with the one ease (`cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.8, 0.2, 1)`) at 120ms for small state changes, 160ms for toasts and dialogs, 200ms for panels, the inspector and the canvas. Layout that moves what is below it (an Idea card's text unfolding) takes 320ms (`--dur-4`) on the fold ease (`--ease-fold`, `cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)`), which starts gently so the move reads rather than jumps, and folds back in 200ms. Honour reduced motion.
**Do** show focus with the 2px accent outline at 1px offset. Rows inside sheets inset it (-2px).
**Do** keep Story pages out of Studio: the Story guidance and house styles never copy the app's tokens.
**Do** give every card kit colour in both themes. A diagram the kit lacks is drawn with the kit's variables (`currentColor`, the hue's ink and line, muted), never fixed colours.
donts: **Don't** add a top bar, a second rail, an app-level tab strip or extra drawers beside the panel. On phones the panel itself is the drawer.

**Don't** set app type above 20px outside the overview's intro, and don't add a display face to the app: the display step is Inter at 600. An Idea card's front is a picture in the card kit, not app type.
**Don't** use the accent for decoration, category colour, large fills or more than one filled button in a view.
**Don't** use shadows outside the resting, lifted and paper set, including hard offset, coloured or glow shadows.
**Don't** add small uppercase labels above titles. Section labels are 11px sentence case in faint 500.
**Don't** use text characters or emoji as icons. Every icon is a lucide glyph.

**Don't** add editing controls to an Idea card, a label saying who a side is for, or a reminder to ask an agent. Agents write both sides, together; people read the picture, open More info for the text, drag outcomes into order, and the menu only archives and deletes.
**Don't** put text-heavy content on a front: about 60 words of running text on the concept's, 40 on an outcome's, and labels of two to five words. Depth belongs on the back.
